original_question: Is it consistent that the positive polarized spectrum has two distinct breaking points below ℵω?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 3.16: Is it consistent that the polarized spectrum includes two breaking points below ℵω? The nearby terminology of a breaking point is introduced immediately above in Problem 3.15, in the setting of the positive spectrum of strong polarized relations on pairs (κ, ω). ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target: it correctly identifies that this is a consistency question about the positive spectrum of polarized partition relations, and it correctly singles out the possibility of two breaking points below ℵω. This matches Problem 3.16 rather than a broader neighboring problem. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
missing_details: The paper is specifically about the strong polarized relation on pairs (κ, ω), not an arbitrary polarized spectrum at other lower cardinals.

The positive relation should be unpacked explicitly: for every coloring c: κ×ω → 2, there exist A ⊆ κ and B ⊆ ω such that |A| = κ, |B| = ω, and c is constant on A×B. This is the notation introduced in Definition 1.1. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
A stand-alone version should say that the relevant spectrum is the set of uncountable cardinals κ for which that strong polarized relation holds.
The draft does not specify that the question is one of consistency with ZFC.

The paper does not formally define 'breaking point'; the nearby context only introduces it informally, so a stand-alone question should explain that these are cardinals where the truth pattern of the positive spectrum changes. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

The nearby context motivating the question uses Theorem 2.6, which controls positivity below the splitting number s; that structural background is omitted from the draft. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

The paper also records the contextual consequence that if θ0 < θ1 < ℵω are such breaking points, then s ≤ θ0 and u ≥ θ1. This is not part of the formal statement, but it is an important nearby constraint. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
refined_question: Is it consistent with ZFC that the spectrum S = {κ ≥ ℵ1 : for every coloring c: κ×ω → 2 there exist A ⊆ κ and B ⊆ ω with |A| = κ and |B| = ω such that c is constant on A×B} has two distinct breaking points below ℵω, i.e. that the truth value of this strong polarized relation changes at two distinct cardinals θ0 < θ1 < ℵω?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Section 3, Problem 3.16. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must identify the spectrum as the Section 3 spectrum for the strong polarized relation on (κ, ω), unpack the arrow notation using Definition 1.1, and use the immediately preceding Problem 3.15 for the paper’s informal notion of a breaking point. Theorem 2.6 is the nearby structural result explaining why this spectrum is being studied in terms of s and why the question is about how complicated its behavior can be. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
